scenarioSurface.capabilityName: Decide which observed artifacts enter the content-addressed capability estate
scenarioSurface.scenarioName: Resolve what provisioning disposition each artifact earns

input.text: classified artifacts and the refinement state each one is declared to hold

outcome.text: a script that has been scenario-shaped is SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION_PENDING, and one that has not is SCENARIO_SHAPING_PENDING, because a provisioned script is preserved evidence and never a discharged responsibility

scenarioSurface.notes:
Provisioning has been performed by a hand-written script since the estate began.
  That script does seven things, and only two of them are effects: it walks a
  directory tree, and it writes bytes. The other five are decisions - admitting a
  batch request, screening artifacts against a secret policy, classifying each
  artifact by its declared extension, resolving what provisioning disposition each
  one earns, and binding the manifest entries that record them. Those five are what
  this capability owns.

  It owns no walk and no scan. The observed artifact set is presented to it, and
  each artifact arrives carrying the policy screen already applied. That is not a
  convenience: the admitted transformation vocabulary has no pattern matching, so a
  capability claiming to screen bytes would be claiming something it cannot perform.
  Screening is testimony. Deciding what that testimony means is governance.

  An artifact carrying any policy finding is rejected unless the batch request
  declares an explicit allowance naming that artifact and that rule. An allowance
  naming no finding is itself a finding, because a blanket allowance is how a secret
  enters an estate that believes it screens.

  Classification is declared, never inferred. An artifact whose extension is absent
  from the declared catalog is rejected rather than guessed at, because a guessed
  media type is how an unreviewable byte acquires a respectable name.

  Coverage is proven. Every artifact the batch selected is either provisioned with a
  content-addressed entry or rejected with a named reason. An artifact that is
  neither is a hole in the account the estate keeps of itself.

  Absence is never normalized. A batch presenting no observed artifacts has not
  provisioned an empty set; it has failed to present its observations.

anyOf.description: One provisioning batch, its observed artifacts, and the artifact catalog that classifies them. Walking a tree and scanning bytes are effects performed elsewhere; what arrives here is observation.

selections.description: What the batch declared it was provisioning. An empty selection set is a failure to declare, never a batch that selected nothing.

policyAllowances.description: Explicit exceptions. Each must name both the artifact and the rule it excuses; an allowance naming neither is unbounded and is itself a finding.

digestShard.description: The content-address shard of the digest. Reported by the observer because the admitted transformation vocabulary cannot take a substring.

policyScreen.description: The secret policy screen already applied to the bytes. Supplied as testimony because pattern matching is not an admitted transformation operation.

declaredArtifactCatalog.description: The declared binding of extension to artifact type, language and media type. Classification is read from here, never inferred.

anyOf.description: The provisioning decision admitted at each downstream scenario boundary, where the carrier is the previously admitted outcome.

schema.title: provisioning-carrier
schema.description: The carrier admitted at each provisioning boundary. Each step observes the accumulated decision and preserves it; no step provisions an artifact another step rejected.

provisionedEntries.description: One content-addressed entry per distinct digest. Two observations of identical bytes bind one entry carrying both sources.

disposition.description: A provisioned script is preserved evidence, never a discharged responsibility.
PROVISIONED only when every observed artifact was either provisioned or explicitly rejected.
